name: Chladni Circular Plate — Free Edge, 432 Hz

comparison_clamped_center.note: Free-edge circular plates produce fundamentally different mode shapes than clamped-center plates. The lowest modes have nodal diameters but NO nodal circles — the entire disc flexes, with the rim free to displace. This is the mode family of cymbals, gongs, and bells.
comparison_clamped_center.frequency_ratio: Free-edge fundamental is approximately 2.5× lower than clamped-center at same dimensions

modes.name: Quadrupole
modes.description: Two nodal diameters, no nodal circles. The fundamental free-edge mode.
modes.sacred: The four-petal form — the first crack in the cosmos
modes.notes: The rim oscillates in a quadrupole pattern: two antinodes pointing up, two pointing down, alternating at 90° intervals. This is the exact mode of a wine glass at its singing frequency.

modes.name: Triskelion
modes.sacred: Six-fold: three crests, three troughs, the hexagonal origin

modes.name: Quadrupole with inner ring
modes.description: Two diameters + one inner nodal circle

modes.name: Decapole
modes.description: Five nodal diameters — the pentagram family
modes.sacred: Ten-fold: the Pythagorean dekad, the completion of number

modes.name: Hexagram with ring
modes.sacred: Star of David enclosed in the wheel

rim_driving.technique: Touch the plate at one point on the rim (this becomes a node). Bow the rim at 90°/m from the touch point.
rim_driving.optimal_rosin: Use quality violin rosin on a cello or bass bow. The slower bow speed relative to violin gives better coupling to the plate's low-frequency modes.

medium.depth_effect: Thicker sand layer (>2 grain diameters) can damp higher modes. Use minimum coverage for cleanest patterns.

acoustic_properties.radiation_efficiency: Free-edge plates are efficient radiators — the rim motion couples well to air. Clamped-center plates are poor radiators (the nodes hold the rim still).

notes: This is the plate geometry of the Tibetan singing bowl (though the bowl is hemispherical rather than flat). The free-edge boundary condition allows the rim to be driven like a bell — struck or continuously bowed. The free-edge modes are also the modes of the cymbals used in orchestral percussion and Buddhist ritual.
